Working closely with customer stakeholders and GitLab team members, you will guide programs from planning through delivery while building trusted relationships across executive, technical, and delivery teams.  Work closely with Engagement Managers and Regional Delivery Managers to support program scoping, review delivery assumptions, and help improve project management processes through quarterly objectives and key results (OKRs)
 What you'll bring
 Experience leading complex programs with multiple interdependent projects, stakeholders, and timelines
 Strong skill in program planning, forecasting, reporting, and communicating delivery metrics clearly to internal and external stakeholders
 Ability to organize, monitor, and manage long-term project budgets, schedules, risks, and dependencies
 Proven ability to build collaborative relationships with customers and partner effectively with Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery teams
 Working knowledge of agile and other project management approaches, with the judgment to apply the right structure to different customer needs
 Ability to develop long-term plans that support customer adoption, transformation, and successful delivery outcomes
 Comfort leading program-level meetings and driving progress across multiple workstreams
 Willingness to complete GitLab Project Management certification within 2 months of starting in the role

 On our Professional Services team, we help customers adopt GitLab effectively by turning strategy into structured delivery. As Program Managers on our team, we bring clarity to large, complex engagements by coordinating people, plans, and processes across multiple workstreams. We work closely with customers, Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery leaders to create practical plans, manage risk, and keep programs moving toward agreed outcomes. Because we operate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, we value clear communication, strong documentation, and ownership. This role is well suited for you if you enjoy building order in complex environments, guiding stakeholders through change, and helping customers make progress on meaningful transformation efforts.

description:

If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.
About the Role:
Camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale. From Hub they manage their clusters and tenants, decide who can do what, and roll changes out across the whole organization. We’re looking for a Senior Product Builder to own the backend and architecture that let Hub manage a whole fleet of clusters. Your first focus will be the mechanism that sends access, secret, tenant and licence changes out to every connected cluster and brings deployments, health and audit records back. From there, you’ll shape Hub’s foundations: its event model, the service boundaries and data model other teams build on, and how Hub behaves when things fail or get upgraded. The platform is your product. Your users are platform administrators, Centres of Excellence and the builders across Camunda who depend on what you create. You’ll join a new two-person pod in our remote-first team. You’ll have real ownership as the person who makes the call, and you’ll build AI-first, from written specs through to production. Our customers run mission-critical processes on Camunda, so your work will matter to them every day.
What You Will Do:
 - Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles
 - Write short design documents for foundational changes, get them reviewed by the teams that depend on them, and turn them into tested, shipped code
 - Design how Hub behaves when things go wrong: offline clusters, partial failures, Hub outages, and clusters being adopted or detached
 - Build the path from clusters back to Hub, starting with deployment inventory, health, audit records and licence status
 - Design Hub's first event and webhook mechanism, so admins and agents can react to changes instead of polling for them
 - Join the pod's rotations and Hub on-call, and help other builders take on backend work through reviews, guidelines and contract tests
What You Will Bring to the Role:
 - Experience building and running backend systems in production that other teams or customers depend on
 - Comfort taking a problem nobody owns yet and turning it into a design, a plan and shipped code
 - Product judgment for technical users: you talk to the people who use your APIs and make trade-offs on their behalf
 - Clear, short writing that lets a remote team review and decide asynchronously
 - Care for how a system behaves when parts of it fail, not only for the happy path
Must Haves:
 - Designed and shipped a control plane or similar system that pushes desired state to many targets. Knows outbox or event-log patterns, idempotent apply, versioning, retries and drift reconciliation
 - Senior backend engineering in Java (API design, relational data models, multi-tenant SaaS services) and hands-on Helm and Kubernetes for self-managed installations
 - Software architecture and failure analysis: partial failure, blast radius, consistency trade-offs. Has debugged production incidents in a distributed system and is ready for on-call
 - Has shaped an API or platform as a product, and writes design docs other teams can build on. Gets agreement across teams without formal authority
 - Builds AI-first from written specifications and checks AI output as carefully as any other code
Nice to Haves:
 - Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools, for example Argo CD
 - OIDC, SCIM and permission models, or secret managers and licence systems
 - Camunda 8 or another workflow or orchestration engine
 - Enough frontend skill to build a thin UI on top of a backend capability

title: Product Builder - Mo (AI health companion)
description:
🤖 WHO WE ARE
We’re building Mo — a health companion for everyone.
We’re a small team within Alan, on a mission to redefine the future of care by democratizing access to medical expertise. We are building Mo, an intelligent, empathetic, multimodal LLM-based conversational AI assistant able to prescribe, triage, and proactively follow up on care.
Imagine giving every person in the world instant, 24/7 access to personalised medical expertise - through chat, voice, or video. That’s what we are building 🤖.
We kicked off the project in 2023, and we have launched Mo to all our french members (1M) in Q1 2026, making it the first safe AI health companion live at scale in Europe.
🚀 WHY WE NEED YOU
Mo’s scope is expanding fast: inside Alan (a new Clinic, new capabilities), across the countries we operate in, and at the interfaces with many other Alan experiences. To get this expansion right, and to keep ownership distributed within the team, we’re looking for a Product Builder to take on a real share of that complexity and ambiguity.
You’ll own end-to-end one slice of Mo’s product scope. Depending on your profile, it could be:
 - 🩺 Mo for reactive care. Build all the integrations between Mo, our Clinic and the healthcare system, and shape how our medical team interacts with members in and through Mo.
 - 🛡️ Mo for insurance. Make Mo the main interface between members and Alan, building on our Support AI agents, across channels and countries.
 - 🌍 Mo global. Adapt Mo to new countries and find the right operating model for each (medical reviews, safety, local features).
 - ➕ Mo as a platform. Make Mo the companion other teams build upon, so our domain experts can ship their own experiences through it.
🎯 IS IT YOU WE’RE LOOKING FOR?
We’re looking for Product Builders with around 5+ years of experience who want to build state-of-the-art AI products and apply them to real-world, high-stakes problems in healthcare.
 - You’ll own a product area end-to-end: problem framing, vision, prioritisation, shipping, and measuring whether we actually help members get and stay better.
 - You’ll work daily with engineers, ML engineers, data, and doctors, at the frontier of LLMs and agentic systems, and see your work in production with real people.
 - You’ll navigate ambiguity and many stakeholders across Alan, and turn it into clear decisions and a focused roadmap.
 - You’ll be hands-on: prototyping, digging into data, reading conversations and evals, getting into the technical details with the team.
 - You’ll contribute to our product culture and help build the team (hiring, interview loops, etc.).
You would be a good fit in Mo if most of this sounds like you:
 - Experience building and shipping a live AI/LLM product
 - Very hands-on, comfortable with technical and data topics (SQL, prototyping, understanding how an LLM system behaves and fails)
 - Interest or experience in one or several medical or prevention themes
 - Product-minded and outcome-driven: you care about impact, not output
 - Self-directed, pragmatic, driven, hard working
 - Humble and still willing to grow (no matter your seniority!)
 - Collaborative, enthusiastic about teamwork, learning, and teaching
 - Fluent in English
 - Ex-engineers and ex-founders are typically a great fit in our team
But above all, we are looking for high potential and curiosity: make sure to show us this when you apply! Everything else is a bonus
🤘 HOW WE DO IT ?
We benefit from Alan’s platform, infrastructure, distribution, and health expertise — but operate with the speed and focus of a startup. At Pencil, we are building the operating system for AI-powered marketing — a SaaS platform that uses Generative AI to redefine how the world's biggest brands plan, produce and deploy advertising. Our mission is to make AI the default in marketing without replacing creative people. A core part of this role is supporting the engineering requests and requirements of our Tier 1 clients. This is a senior craft role. It doesn't own a product area and doesn't manage engineers directly. title: Senior Product Manager (Workflows & Integrations)

ABOUT US
At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.
THE ROLE
Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.
You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.
You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

 - Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

 - Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.
 - Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.
 - Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.
 - Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.
 - Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.
 - Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.
 - Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.
 - Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.
 - Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.
YOUR BACKGROUND
You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:

 - Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability.

description:
At Forbes Advisor, our mission is to help readers turn their aspirations into reality. We arm people with trusted advice and guidance so they can make informed decisions they feel confident in and get back to doing the things they care about most.
We are an experienced team of industry experts dedicated to helping readers make smart decisions and choose the right products with ease. The team brings rich industry knowledge to Forbes Advisor's global coverage of consumer credit, debt, health, home improvement, banking, investing, credit cards, small business, education, insurance, loans, real estate and travel.
 About The Role
 Forbes Advisor is investing in the platform and technology that power our business, and we’re looking for a best-in-class Technical Product Manager to help drive it forward. This hands-on role will take ownership of the technical product initiatives that keep our platform secure, scalable and ready for what’s next. You’ll become the go-to person for turning strategic goals into technical reality – shaping the architecture, capabilities and tooling that let every team move faster. Above all, you’ll deliver solutions that create real, measurable value.
Great products are built on great foundations – so getting the technical detail right is everything. You’ll own the development lifecycle end to end, from early-stage requirements through delivery and ongoing optimisation, making sure what we build is robust today and extensible tomorrow.
You’ll bring technical product initiatives to life across the business, working alongside functions including Engineering, Data and Analytics, Privacy & Security, Compliance and the wider Product team. You’ll turn business goals and technical opportunity into a clear, prioritised roadmap, keeping feasibility, scalability and ROI at the centre of every decision.
The person we’re looking for is a genuine all-rounder who’s as comfortable in a technical architecture discussion as in a stakeholder update. You’re a self-starter and an exemplary communicator who bridges the gap between technical and non-technical teams and reliably delivers what matters most.
 Responsibilities
 Strategy & roadmap
 Own the product strategy and roadmap for technical initiatives across the business, aligned to overall business goals – balancing innovation with execution readiness and available technical capacity. 
 Build and maintain a prioritised, transparent backlog, ensuring the roadmap reflects the evolving needs of the business and the realities of technical delivery. 
 Requirements & Delivery
 Lead the development lifecycle of technical product initiatives, from early-stage requirements gathering through delivery and ongoing optimisation. 
 Collaborate with business stakeholders to turn strategic goals into clear functional and non-functional requirements. 
 Translate complex business needs into detailed technical specifications and user stories that engineering teams can implement effectively and efficiently. 
 Architecture, platform & scalability
 Work hand-in-hand with technical leads to shape platform architecture, prioritise infrastructure improvements, and ensure systems are secure, scalable and extensible. 
 Help define the internal processes and documentation standards that enable repeatable, scalable technical delivery across multiple teams and initiatives. 
 AI, automation & data
 Partner closely with Data and Analytics to identify where AI, automation or intelligent tooling can enhance workflows and user experience. 
 Evaluate use cases on feasibility, technical constraints and ROI, and turn the strongest into delivered capabilities that move the numbers that matter. 
 Stakeholder communication
 Serve as the communication bridge between technical and non-technical teams, keeping everyone aligned on product vision, delivery status and the technical trade-offs being made.
